raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview The FlashInfer sparse MLA kernel silently skips attention for every token of a forward pass with more than 65535 tokens (e.g. any full prefill step at `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`), returning uninitialized memory. This PR launches it in chunks of at most 65535 tokens that write into one preallocated output. Root cause on the FlashInfer side: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3125. ## Claims - Fixes the silent skip for `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` (**DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5 / GLM-5.3 DSA layers**) and for the prefill of `FLASHATTN_MLA_SPARSE` (FA4), which delegates prefill to the same kernel. Covers prefill, decode, mixed steps and DCP. - Steps with <= 65535 tokens issue the same single launch as before (decode and CUDA graphs are unchanged). - No extra memory: chunks write into slices of one output (and LSE) buffer. - The DCP softmax-stats workspace is sized for one launch (<= 65535 tokens) instead of `max_num_batched_tokens`. ## Validation | Check | Base (main) | This PR | |---|---|---| | New `test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_attends_tokens_past_grid_limit` (69635 tokens, rope and no-rope), SM10x | 2/2 fail (NaN past token 65535) | 2/2 pass | | 40-shot GSM8K, GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4, DEP2, `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`, 2 greedy runs | ~3 points below the unaffected baseline; server log full of `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE ... fmhaKernels.cuh` | at the unaffected baseline (within run-to-run spread); no launch errors | | 4 TP1 prefill workers at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` + DEP4 decode, 8K/1K sa-bench, C512/C1024 | prefill OOM with an earlier chunk + `torch.cat` version of this fix | no OOM; throughput at parity with that version, median TTFT slightly lower | | RULER-64K (NeMo-Skills, 13 tasks x 100), same server shape, `--max-model-len 131072` | overall ~35 points below this PR; NIAH / variable tracking 11-82 points lower per task; ~7.7K `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE ... fmhaKernels.cuh` lines while serving | NIAH (8 tasks) and variable tracking all at or near 100%; no launch errors | Run on SM107 GPUs; end-to-end results are relative. - The 40-shot GSM8K prompts are 7-8K tokens, above the DSA top-k, so sparse MLA runs. 5-shot GSM8K does not show the bug, because short prompts take the dense MHA prefill path. - The DCP/LSE path (one launch per chunk with an `lse` slice) was also checked against a PyTorch reference at 69635 tokens. That ran outside the committed tests, because DCP needs more than one GPU. ```bash pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_workspace.py \ -k "past_grid_limit or model_scale or workspace or dcp_size" ```
Before / after test output Base (main 51d2a8559): ``` E Mismatched elements: 6884 / 8192 (84.0%) E Greatest absolute difference: nan at index (0, 52) (up to 0.02 allowed) E Mismatched elements: 6850 / 8192 (83.6%) E Greatest absolute difference: nan at index (0, 282) (up to 0.02 allowed) FAILED tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_attends_tokens_past_grid_limit[128-64-128] FAILED tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_attends_tokens_past_grid_limit[256-0-256] FAILED tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_workspace.py::test_dcp_size_is_capped_at_one_launch 3 failed, 20 passed, 1883 deselected, 18 warnings in 52.12s ``` This PR: ``` 23 passed, 1883 deselected, 18 warnings in 52.08s ```
Why not FlashInfer's cum_seq_lens_q (#3131 / #3238)? Measured at kernel level (FP8 KV, top-k 2048, 16 and 64 heads, 1 to 131072 tokens): - trtllm-gen cannot return the LSE with `cum_seq_lens_q`, and DCP needs it. - `seq_lens` becomes per request. The static-sparse (rope) path uses it as each token's active top-k length, so rows shorter than the top-k width attend the `-1` padding and give wrong outputs. - Grouping tokens by real request launches `num_reqs x max_q_len` CTAs: one long prefill plus 511 decodes ran ~9.5x slower. - Packing tokens into uniform pseudo-requests (no-rope, no LSE) is bit-exact but no faster (within 1%): the MLA generation kernels still run one CTA per token. - For comparison, chunked launches cost the same per token as one launch. Chunk + `torch.cat` is 2-11% slower, and its extra output copy (8 GiB at 65536 tokens with 64 heads) is outside vLLM's memory profile.
## Details **Root cause.** `FlashInferMLASparseImpl._forward_mqa_kernel` passes every query token to `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` as its own request (`q.unsqueeze(1)`, `topk_indices.unsqueeze(1)`), and trtllm-gen maps requests to `gridDim.z`, whose CUDA limit is 65535. A larger launch makes `cuLaunchKernelEx` return `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE`, which FlashInfer only prints to stderr. Found with a profile that showed zero sparse-MLA kernels in every 65536-token step. **Fix.** Allocate `out` (and `lse`) once and call the kernel on row slices of at most 65535 tokens, passing the matching `out` / `lse` slices. FlashInfer accepts caller-owned output, so no copy is needed. The trtllm-gen softmax-stats slab is carved per launch, so the DCP workspace only needs to cover one launch. **Limitations.** Steps with more than 65535 tokens issue one extra kernel launch per additional chunk. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate and write this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above. Not a duplicate: no open vLLM PR touches this backend's 65535-token limit (searched "flashinfer_mla_sparse", "65535 flashinfer", "cum_seq_lens_q"). ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

     assert recorded_scale != kv_lora_rank**-0.5
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100),
+    reason="trtllm-gen sparse MLA requires SM10x",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("qk_nope_head_dim", "qk_rope_head_dim", "v_head_dim"),
+    [(128, 64, 128), (256, 0, 256)],
+)
+def test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_attends_tokens_past_grid_limit(
+    default_vllm_config, dist_init, qk_nope_head_dim, qk_rope_head_dim, v_head_dim
+):
+    """trtllm-gen maps each token to gridDim.z (limit 65535); a larger step,
+    e.g. a 64K-token prefill, must still attend every token."""
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    num_tokens, num_heads, kv_lora_rank, topk, block_size = (
+        65536 + 4099,
+        16,
+        512,
+        128,
+        64,
+    )
+    head_size = kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim
+    impl = FlashInferMLASparseImpl(
+        num_heads=num_heads,
+        head_size=head_size,
+        scale=head_size**-0.5,
+        num_kv_heads=1,
+        alibi_slopes=None,
+        sliding_window=None,
+        kv_cache_dtype="auto",
+        logits_soft_cap=None,
+        attn_type="decoder",
+        kv_sharing_target_layer_name=None,
+        q_lora_rank=None,
+        kv_lora_rank=kv_lora_rank,
+        qk_nope_head_dim=qk_nope_head_dim,
+        qk_rope_head_dim=qk_rope_head_dim,
+        qk_head_dim=qk_nope_head_dim + qk_rope_head_dim,
+        v_head_dim=v_head_dim,
+        kv_b_proj=ColumnParallelLinear(
+            kv_lora_rank, num_heads * (qk_nope_head_dim + v_head_dim), bias=False
+        ),
+    )
+    gen = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(0)
+    kv_cache = (
+        torch.rand(64, block_size, head_size, generator=gen, device=device) - 0.5
+    ).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    q = (
+        torch.rand(num_tokens, num_heads, head_size, generator=gen, device=device) - 0.5
+    ).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    # Mixed active lengths, valid indices first and -1 padding after, as the
+    # index converters produce.
+    valid_counts = torch.randint(
+        1, topk + 1, (num_tokens,), generator=gen, device=device, dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    valid_counts[::3] = topk
+    topk_indices = torch.randint(
+        0,
+        kv_cache.shape[0] * block_size,
+        (num_tokens, topk),
+        generator=gen,
+        device=device,
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+    )
+    slots = torch.arange(topk, device=device)
+    topk_indices.masked_fill_(slots[None, :] >= valid_counts[:, None], -1)
+
+    out, lse = impl._forward_mqa_kernel(
+        q,
+        kv_cache,
+        topk_indices,
+        valid_counts,
+        layer=SimpleNamespace(),
+        block_size=block_size,
+        is_decode=False,
+    )
+
+    assert lse is None
+    kv_rows = kv_cache.view(-1, head_size).float()
+    # Both sides of the 65535 boundary, the ends, and a sweep in between.
+    rows = sorted({0, 65534, 65535, 65536, num_tokens - 1, *range(0, num_tokens, 997)})
+    for t in rows:
+        kv = kv_rows[topk_indices[t, : valid_counts[t]].long()]
+        scores = q[t].float() @ kv.T * impl.scale
+        ref = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1) @ kv[:, :kv_lora_rank]
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out[t].float(), ref, atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+
+
